answer: Because the mirror stake is held until the mesa settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the spiral audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 27% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A farm running 108 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap.
